name: ntfy
description: Simple HTTP-based pub-sub notification service. Send push notifications to your phone or desktop via scripts.
summary: ntfy has been actively releasing updates through mid-2026, with the latest being v2.28.0 (2026-08-27, https://github.com/binwiederhier/ntfy/releases/tag/v2.28.0), a hardening release that caps cache replay sizes at 10 MB per topic, enforces new size limits on message titles (1 KB) and tags (512 bytes), and applies the visitor bandwidth budget to poll requests. v2.27.0 (2026-08-04) dropped the 'experimental' label from PostgreSQL support, added email-based login, and hardened the message templating engine. Earlier releases added password reset via magic links (v2.25.0), a fail2ban-compatible abuse ban-feed (v2.26.3), and a CPU DoS fix for message templates (v2.26.0).

answers.What is the current license?: Apache 2.0 (server) and GPL-2.0 (client) — dual-licensed; see repository for details
answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes — multiple releases in 2026, most recently v2.28.0 on 2026-08-27
answers.Does it support authentication and acces: Yes — username/password auth, access tokens, email-based login, and topic-level access control
answers.Is there a hosted cloud version availabl: Yes — ntfy.sh is the official hosted cloud instance

breaking_excerpts: Message title now limited to 1 KB and all tags combined to 512 bytes; requests exceeding these limits are rejected with HTTP 400 (error codes 40057/40058).
Cache replay capped at 10 MB per topic per poll request; truncated responses include X-Messages-Truncated: 1 header — previously unbounded.
Message cache databases from ntfy older than v1.10.0 (November 2021) can no longer be migrated; must upgrade via an older ntfy version first or delete the cache database.

alternatives.name: Pushover
alternatives.review: Paid SaaS, simple API, iOS/Android apps.

alternatives.name: Gotify
alternatives.review: Self-hosted only, real-time push via WebSocket.

alternatives.name: Apprise
alternatives.review: Apprise is a library/CLI supporting 80+ notification services rather than a standalone server, making it more flexible but requiring more integration effort than ntfy.

alternatives.name: Pushbullet
alternatives.review: Pushbullet offers cross-device notifications with file sharing features but is a proprietary cloud service with rate-limited free tier and no self-hosting.

alternatives.name: Ntfy (self-hosted) vs Bark
alternatives.review: Bark is a lightweight iOS-only self-hosted push notification tool that is simpler to deploy but limited to Apple devices compared to ntfy's cross-platform support.
